text:
ana: Quick sync — product just finalized the structured-output + function-calling spec for the next release. Need SDK + docs alignment before we cut release candidate. Main asks from customers: typed outputs (TS + py dataclasses), clear examples for tool flows, changelog guidance, and backward-compatible API surface. Who can drive?
tyler: I can triage surface gaps. main question: do we expose native typed response objects or keep a raw dict + helper constructors?
marta: customers prefer typed objects for autocomplete/IDE UX. but we need a clear migration path. i'd vote for typed models in TS + optional dataclasses in py.
sam: re: py dataclasses — need to confirm import paths and serialization hooks for nested tool results. also think about validation: lightweight pydantic v2?
kevin: +1 to optional pydantic wrappers. keep core SDK returning raw payloads by default to avoid surprising behavior and provide typed helpers behind a feature flag.
ana: decision proposal: default behavior stays raw JSON; add "from_schema" typed constructors in both clients and generate type defs from the API schemas. feature flag: "typed_output" for early adopters. can we ship examples and changelog notes in the same PR?
tyler: timeline check — product wants this in the 2.1 milestone (release in ~3 weeks). to hit that we'll need: spec->typegen, SDK changes, docs examples, examples repo updates, changelog entry. estimate: 1.5w engineering, 3d docs, 2d QA. tight but doable if we parallelize.
marta: blocked items: 1) stable schema for structured output + tool call payloads; 2) typegen infra for python (we have TS generation in ci). status: product finalized schema but need small tweaks for optional fields.
kevin: i'll pick up the python typegen work if somebody can own the ts side. sam can you confirm pydantic vs dataclasses?
sam: i can prototype a dataclass + pydantic wrapper pattern today. if we rely on stdlib dataclasses for runtime footprint and provide optional pydantic for validation, we should be fine.
docs-bot: FYI — need at least 3 example snippets: chat + function call, streaming structured output, embeddings->rerank typed pipeline. each example must include expected SDK call, typed response usage, and minimal test.
ana: action items: @tyler own TS typegen + SDK surface changes (due in 7 days). @kevin own py typegen + runtime helpers (due in 7 days). @marta own docs examples + changelog draft (due in 5 days). @sam prototype dataclass pattern (due 2 days). i'll coordinate release checklist and QA.
tyler: quick question on API naming — product added top-level field "structured_output_schema" on responses. shall we map that to generated types as Response.Structured? prefer flattened names or nested?
marta: prefer nested Response.structured_output to avoid collisions with other fields. docs examples will show pattern.
kevin: implementation note: in python we'll generate classes under redwood.sdk.types.response.StructuredOutput for autocompletion. provide from_dict() / to_dict() helpers.
sam: code sketch (py) in thread:
```
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Optional, List

@dataclass
class ToolResult:
    name: str
    output: str
    metadata: Optional[dict] = None

@dataclass
class StructuredOutput:
    content: str
    tools: Optional[List[ToolResult]] = None

# usage
resp = client.chat.create(...)
so = StructuredOutput.from_dict(resp["structured_output"])  # helper generated
print(so.tools[0].name)
```

marta: add TS sketch too.
tyler: TS sketch:
```
export type ToolResult = { name: string; output: string; metadata?: Record<string, unknown> }
export type StructuredOutput = { content: string; tools?: ToolResult[] }

const resp = await client.chat.create(...)
const so = StructuredOutput.from(resp.structured_output) // generated helper
```

ana: docs guidance: include a section "Migration from raw payloads" showing both patterns (raw access vs typed wrappers). also include a note: typed_output is opt-in and subject to schema changes during beta.
marta: changelog wording suggestion: "Add opt-in typed SDK helpers for structured output and function-calling. Defaults remain unchanged. See migration guide."
kevin: QA notes: add unit tests that exercise serialization + roundtrip of generated types, and an integration test in examples repo that runs a mock tool call.
sam: will push prototype by EOD.
tyler: i'll wire up TS generation in ci and add a feature-flag gate that flips on in the rc.
ana: ok good. follow-ups: if any customer asks for stable typing guarantee, we'll direct them to Dedicated/Private enterprise contract for stronger compatibility SLAs. for public API keep opt-in.
marta: can we get the marketing/copy team to review changelog line? small ask — i'll ping them.
kevin: one more thing: update SDK changelog process to include a "typegen version" line so we can track schema -> client mapping changes.
ana: summary: agreed approach = raw default + optional generated typed helpers, feature flaged typed_output, TS + py typegen, docs examples + migration guide, changelog + tests. owners assigned. I'll create checklist in GH and link here.
docs-bot: created GH issue #1245: "SDK typed-output launch checklist" and linked to this thread.
ana: perfect — thanks everyone. check-ins mid-week. :thumbsup:
